surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the exposure of the substrate to TBTDEN, which generates a saturated mono-layer, followed by a remote hydrogen plasma step to reduce the mono-layer to form NbN. The process includes purge steps with argon to avoid additional chemical vapor deposition.
evidence: At the ﬁrst step the substrate surface is exposed to TBTDEN, which generates a saturated mono-layer on the substrate. Then, the residual TBTDEN is purged with argon to avoid additional chemical vapor deposition. The mono-layer is, at the third step, reduced by a remote hydrogen plasma to form a mono-layer of NbN, followed by the fourth step of a second argon purge.
